text:
maria: Heads-up — onboarding Cassiopeia's LoRA adapter. Merge applied to redwood-13b-v1. Quick eval pack failing on tokenization-sensitive prompts, numbers/dates look garbled.

jon: Can you paste the tokenizer config and the exact merge command you used?

maria: Merge command was: `merge_lora --base redwood-13b-v1 --adapter cassiopeia/lora-v2 --out /tmp/cassiopeia-merged`. Tokenizer snippet shows conflicting vocab sizes: cassiopeia tokenizer vocab_size=50257 vs base=50400.

li: If vocab sizes differ we either remap ids or stitch with token alignment. Did you try `hf-remap` or adapter-stitch align?

maria: Quick remap attempt:
```
hf-remap --from cassiopeia/tokenizer.json --to redwood/tokenizer.json --out remap.json
```
Ran int4 quant smoke after remap — eval-bot reports +3% hallucination on date prompts.

eval-bot: EVAL REPORT: model=cassiopeia-merged quant=int4 batch=8
metrics: {"exact_match": "-1.2%", "hallucination": "+3.1%", "avg_latency_ms": "68"}
logs: /evals/cassiopeia/pack-031.log

samira: Could be kv-cache alignment after remap + int4 kernels. Can you repro on float16 to isolate quant error?

maria: float16 run looks clean (hallucination -0.2%). Also noticed adapter trained with max_seq=1024 while base uses 2048 — possible positional embedding mismatch.

jon: Two independent issues: tokenizer/vocab remap and pos-emb mismatch. For a quick unblock try adapter-stitch with `--force-pos-rescale --align-tokens` and rerun int4 smoke.

maria: Running stitch now: 
```
adapter-stitch --base redwood-13b-v1 --adapter cassiopeia/lora-v2 --align-tokens --force-pos-rescale --quant int4 --out /tmp/cass-stitched
```
ETA ~12m.

deploy-bot: deploy scheduled: cassiopeia-smoke-int4 -> staging in 15m (canary 10%).

li: If stitch fixes it, add onboarding checklist item: "ensure adapter seq_len <= base or rescale pos embeddings; verify vocab remap".

samira: :thumbsup: Also add a small automated sanity set for date/number normalization to the quick eval pack.

maria: Thanks — will post results + diff once stitch finishes.
